qt: to the Commission Barbara Bonte (PfE) Subject:

On 18 March 2026 the Commission presented its proposal for EU Inc., an optional 28th company law regime that will stand alongside the existing national legal forms. The Commission is basing its proposal on Article 114 TFEU and is therefore treating it as a measure that contributes to the harmonisation of the internal market. In its judgment in Case C-436/03, Parliament v Council, the Court of Justice ruled, however, that introducing a new European legal form alongside the existing national legal forms could not be regarded as a harmonisation measure under what was then Article 95 of the EC Treaty, now Article 114 TFEU. In that case the Court accepted what was then Article 308 EC, now Article 352 TFEU, as a legal basis. The Commission is therefore, at the very least, creating the impression of trying to circumvent the principle of unanimity in the Council. How does the Commission justify the choice of Article 114 TFEU as the legal basis for EU Inc., in the light of judgment C-436/03, and why does it believe that Article 352 TFEU — which requires unanimity in the Council — does not apply in this case?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.10.2026) The chosen legal basis of the proposed Regulation on the ‘28th regime corporate legal framework – EU Inc.’ reflects the aim and content of the proposal, as explained in the Explanatory memorandum1. Indeed, the proposal aims at improving the functioning of the internal market and reducing fragmentation by creating a harmonised corporate legal framework which enables businesses to attract investment and grow, by enhancing and facilitating the free movement of capital by providing digital and harmonised rules and procedures that enable both EU and third country investors to invest in EU Inc. companies, and prohibiting the imposition of certain discriminatory or disproportionate requirements. The EU Inc. proposal approximates the laws of the Member States by creating a harmonised company legal form embedded within the legal order of each Member State. It is therefore a national company legal form, not a supranational one. Member States are required to modify their national law to accommodate this new national form. The proposal further provides that an EU Inc. shall carry out cross-border conversions, divisions and mergers in accordance with Chapters I, II and IV of Directive (EU) 2017/1132, in the same way as existing national company forms. In view of this, the ruling in Case C-436/03 does not apply to the ‘EU Inc.’ Regulation.
1 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the 28th regime corporate legal
